role.altitude: The week is still the classroom: keeping order, answering, and teaching the plan that was left. Less of it is hunting that plan and rewriting a name already on the list.
reach: The absent teacher reads what was taught.
A pupil hears the rule that applies.
skills_to_grow: Reject a plan page that is the wrong lesson
Refuse a present mark for a pupil they did not see
Keep order without a log of the room
role.ambitious_version: Before the lesson the absent teacher's plan is open, the class list is the register, and the note of what was taught is the ticked plan. They still keep order, still answer, and still teach the hour.

steps.what: Read the school and class rules the list opens.
Notice a breach and decide what the room's order requires.
Tell the class the rule that applies and keep the room.
Enforce the rule and maintain order in the classroom.
Write the incident line of what was seen.
Send the office the note of the incident.

tasks.design: Noticing a breach, telling the class and keeping order stay as they are. The rules for this class open in {DOCS} from the list the regular teacher and the school left, and an incident line in {OTHER} fills the pupil from the enrolment list and the rule from that list, so the substitute types only what they saw. Nothing watches the room, and the office note in {EMAIL} stays the same length.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rule sheet was hunted at the start of the class, and an incident line repeated the pupil's name and the rule.
tasks.enabler_now: The school rule list and the class list can open with the class, so the substitute types only what they saw.
tasks.still_hard: What a breach means in that moment, and what will keep the room steady, is the substitute's call.
tasks.human_edge: The substitute is in the room and can tell a lapse from a pupil who needs help.
tasks.altitude: The room stays the same length. The shorter piece is finding the rule sheet and retyping a pupil and a rule.

reach.learn: The line they hear is the school rule the list already held.
The line names the pupil from the class list and the rule from the school list, plus what the substitute saw.

evidence.claim: A tutoring firm with a works council needs consent for staff-data rules and for tools that can monitor tutors, such as session logs.
Tutors hold minors' grades and support needs; the basis is a contract, parents are informed, and data is minimised.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one class, one day, in a school. This is not a civic-integration course, not a studio class, and not a drafted course. The room is in person, not a meeting, so the in-person share is 90 against a prior of 90.7 that was labelled as meetings.

Rule-list contract, produced by school leadership and the regular teacher, outside this task: rule id and a short line. The list opens with the class, which is why the read drops to 85 percent; they still read it. If the list is empty, the sheet on the wall is the fallback and the read is not shorter.

Incident contract: pupil id and name are produced by enrolment, outside this task; rule id is produced by the rule list. The substitute is the producer of what was seen, and that sentence is counted in the incident step, which is why it stays at 70 percent. If either list is empty they type the pupil and the rule as well.

The office note is unchanged because the design does not shorten that writing. Nothing watches the room, and there is no log of the substitute. The prior clear gain of 0.01 matches a small net. No model reads behavior. Upkeep of 0.3 hours per 100 is correcting one incident filed on the wrong pupil.
unknowns: Whether this school stores a rule list with a rule id and a short line.
Whether the office wants the incident line the same day.
research_questions: How often is the rule sheet missing, so the read is not shorter?
How often is an incident filed on the wrong pupil?

already_counted.description: Reading the rules once the list is open.
Telling the class the rule, unchanged.
Enforcing the rule in the room, unchanged.
Typing what was seen on the incident line.

incremental.description: Correct one incident filed on the wrong pupil. The sentence of what was seen stays in the incident step.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A day when the rules are on the wall and the incident is handwritten lands near 0. A day when the rules open and the pupil and the rule fill lands near 1. The room stays full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Hear the students' questions in the room.
Open the plan page this question sits on.
Answer the students and watch whether it landed.
Send the absent teacher the question that stayed open.

tasks.design: Hearing the question and answering it stay as they are. The plan page the absent teacher stored in {DOCS} opens for this class and period, and the substitute still reads it before answering. No suggestion is spoken for them, and a note in {EMAIL} about a question that stayed open is unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: The page of the plan the question was about was hunted in a folder while the class waited.
tasks.enabler_now: The absent teacher's stored plan can open on the class and the period, so the page is there to read.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the answer landed, and what to say when the plan does not cover the question, stays with the substitute.
tasks.human_edge: The substitute hears the question and can tell a puzzled look from a pupil who is finished.
tasks.altitude: The answer stays spoken and full length. The shorter piece is hunting the page of the plan the question is about.

reach.learn: The answer comes from the substitute, after they have read the page the absent teacher left.

reach.task: Read a question that stayed open
reach.learn: The note is the question the substitute could not close from the plan.

evidence.claim: In the Tutor CoPilot trial, live suggestions to about 900 tutors and 1,800 K-12 pupils raised topic mastery by 4 percentage points, 9 for lower-rated tutors, at about $20 per tutor a year. The trial was preregistered and randomised.
Tutors in that trial flagged suggestions that were not grade-appropriate.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one class, one day. Hearing and answering stay in the room. The in-person share is 80 against a prior of 77.7 labelled as meetings. This is a school substitute, not a live tutor programme.

Plan-page contract, produced by the absent teacher, outside this task: class, period, page or activity id, and the text of the activity. Opening the plan shows the page for this class and period, which is why the lookup drops to 80 percent; they still read it. If the plan is empty or the wrong period, the paper folder is the fallback.

The question is heard, not captured as a field. No suggestion is spoken. The prior clear gain of 0.54, and the prior that a model is needed, are about having an answer to hand. A stored plan only partly supplies that, and the spoken answer stays full length. The trial above measured mastery, not minutes of this answer, and that figure is not this range.
The cover note is unchanged because the design does not shorten that writing. Upkeep of 0.5 hours per 100 is reopening the wrong period's plan and finding the page.
unknowns: Whether the absent teacher stores the plan with class, period and a page.
How often the stored plan does not cover the question the pupil asked.
research_questions: How often is the opened page the wrong period?
Does an open page change the length of the spoken answer?

already_counted.description: Reading the plan page once it is open.

incremental.description: Reopen the wrong period's plan and find the page. The spoken answer stays in the answer step.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A paper plan, hunted while the class waits, lands near 0.5. A day when the page opens lands near 2. The spoken answer stays full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Follow the absent teacher's lesson plan

steps.what: Read the lesson plans designed by the absent teachers.
Follow that lesson in the order the plan sets.
Tick each activity done or skipped on the plan.
Send the absent teacher the stored note of the lesson.

tasks.design: Teaching the lesson stays the same length. The lesson plans designed by the absent teachers open in {DOCS} for this class and period, and each activity they wrote is a line the substitute ticks, with a sentence only when something was skipped. The note in {EMAIL} to the absent teacher sends that stored list rather than a retyped day.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan was a prose page on the desk, and the note of the day was rewritten for the absent teacher.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored plan can open for this class and period, and each activity the absent teacher wrote can be a line to tick.
tasks.still_hard: Teaching the hour, and deciding to skip a line the room cannot do, stays with the substitute.
tasks.human_edge: The substitute sees whether the class can do the next activity.
tasks.altitude: The lesson stays the same length. The shorter piece is finding the plan and rewriting activities that were already lines.

reach.learn: The note is the ticked plan, with a sentence only where a line was skipped.

reach.task: Do the lesson that was left
reach.learn: The hour follows the plan the absent teacher wrote, in that order.

evidence.claim: Teaching stays with the person, including a short-term substitute following a plan left for the class.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one class, one day. The substitute follows a plan and does not draft one. The in-person share is 74 against a prior of 74.9 labelled as meetings. The prior clear gain of 0.09 is not a reason to shorten the lesson.

Plan contract, produced by the absent teacher, outside this task: class, period, activity id, activity line and materials. The plan opens for this class and period, which is why the read drops to 85 percent; they still read it. A prose page on the desk is the fallback, and then they write a paragraph instead of ticking.

Tick contract: each activity line is produced by the absent teacher. The substitute is the producer of done or skipped, counted in the tick step, which stays at 70 percent because a prose plan still needs a paragraph. The note inserts the link to that ticked list, which is why the note drops to 85 percent; they still write one line if the link is missing.
Upkeep of 0.5 hours per 100 is fixing a tick on the wrong activity when the plan lines were unclear. Nothing drafts a new plan and nothing rewrites the level of the text.
unknowns: Whether the absent teacher's plan is stored as lines or as prose.
Whether the absent teacher reads the ticked note.
research_questions: How often is the plan prose, so the tick becomes a paragraph?
How often is a tick on the wrong activity?

already_counted.description: Reading the plan once it is open.
Ticking done or skipped, or writing the paragraph when the plan is prose.
Writing the one line with the stored note.

incremental.description: Fix a tick on the wrong activity when the plan lines were unclear. Teaching the hour stays in the lesson step.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A prose plan they rewrite as a paragraph lands near 1. A day when the lines tick and the link sends lands near 3. The lesson stays full length.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take attendance and keep the record

steps.what: Take class attendance by noticing who is present.
Mark each pupil present or absent on the class list.
Maintain the attendance records by storing the marked list.
Send the completed register to the school office.

tasks.design: Noticing who is present stays the full round of the room. The class list in {OTHER} comes from enrolment, with pupil and class already on the row, and the substitute sets present or absent on each row; a blank list means they write the name. Closing the list fills the date and the class from the timetable, and that marked list is the attendance record sent on in {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The name was written again on a blank register, and the date and class were retyped at the top.
tasks.enabler_now: Enrolment already holds the class list, and the timetable already holds the date and the class.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing who is actually in the room, including a pupil who arrived late, stays with the substitute.
tasks.human_edge: The substitute can tell a pupil who is present from a name on a list.
tasks.altitude: Noticing who is here stays the full round. The shorter piece is writing a name the list already has, and the date at the top.

reach.learn: The register is the class list with present or absent set by the substitute who was in the room.
Absence is the flag the substitute set after looking, not a score.

evidence.claim: Momoyoga keeps class attendance reports and names no AI.
AI that admits learners, evaluates learning outcomes or monitors tests in educational and vocational training institutions at all levels is high-risk, and those duties apply from 2 December 2027.
A tutoring firm with a works council needs consent for staff-data rules and for tools that can monitor tutors, such as session logs.
Tutors hold minors' grades and support needs; the basis is a contract, parents are informed, and data is minimised. A class register that names pupils is personal data.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: one class, one day, in a school. The room check is in person, so the in-person share is 62 against a prior of 64 labelled as meetings. The prior that most of this could be gained, and the prior chance a model helps, do not remove the round of the room.

Class-list contract, produced by enrolment at the school office, outside this task: pupil id, name and class. The name is already on the row, which is why marking drops to 95 percent; they still set every present or absent flag. The substitute is the producer of present, absent or late, from what they noticed in the room, and that setting is counted in the mark step. A blank list means they write the name.

Header contract, produced by the school office timetable, outside this task: date, class and period. The marker is the logged-in substitute. They still confirm unmarked rows, which is why closing stays at 60 percent. The unmarked-row count is derived from the flags just set, not a separate capture. If the timetable is empty they type the header.

The office mail is unchanged because the design does not shorten that writing. The register stores present or absent on the existing list and does not evaluate a learning outcome or monitor a test. Nothing watches the room. Absence of a pupil is confidential. Upkeep of 0.4 hours per 100 is correcting a present flag set on the wrong row.
unknowns: Whether enrolment can supply this class list with pupil id, name and class.
Whether the office already receives the register by mail.
research_questions: How often is the class list blank, so the name is written by hand?
How often is a present flag on the wrong row?

already_counted.description: Setting present or absent on each row.
Confirming unmarked rows and storing the list.

incremental.description: Correct a present flag set on the wrong row. Noticing who is here stays in the room step.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A blank paper register lands near 0.5. A day when the names are already on the list and the header fills lands near 2.5. Noticing who is here stays the full round.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
